title: Prove machine-session reads through typed backend answers

intentCoverage.report:
# Dough Intent Coverage: fresh ask through the production HTTP adapter

**Verdict: Caught** (by the e2e check only; the six backend session-read specs never reach the faulted path).

## Target
- Story: `.planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#renovate-remaining-backend-families-after-browser-reporter`; plan `.planning/slice-plans/829-prove-machine-session-reads-through-typed-answers/PLAN.md` (G2/G5, slices 4-5).
- Revision: `0c7ad7e2c6019d0b736e8e04ff4218ee61944e10` (branch `claude/prove-machine-session-reads-through-typed-backen`), in an isolated detached scratch worktree at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/2fd37dfe/tmp/ic-scratch`. `npm ci` was run there, and the worktree was clean before the probe.
- Promise: "A fresh ask can see a changed Codex observation while an ordinary ask still reuses a held observation." The faulted half is the fresh ask. Admission happens in `sessionsRequest` (`dashboard/server/sessionsAdmission.ts`), and the answer comes from `MachineSessionObservation.answerFor`. The production adapter that joins the two is `dashboard/server/launchBoundaryAnswer.ts` `case "sessions"`.

## Fault (one edit, no fixtures or assertions touched)
`dashboard/server/launchBoundaryAnswer.ts` line 158:
`(signal) => sessions.answerFor(request, signal)` -> `(signal) => sessions.answerFor({ ...request, fresh: false }, signal)`
This drops the admitted `fresh` at the HTTP adapter. An EXIT trap undid the edit with `git checkout --` on that one file.

## Runs (the same commands for baseline, fault and restore)
1. Backend: `env -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard:backend -- 'backend-tests/sessions/(agent-launch-session-listing|agent-launch-sessions-(encoding|fresh|history|listing|unchanged))\.spec\.ts'`
2. E2E: `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES OPEN_DOUGH_E2E_PROOF_RECORD=<tmp>.json npm run test:e2e -- agent-launch-host-switch-fresh.spec.ts --workers=1`. The quiet reporter prints nothing when the run passes, so a proof record confirmed that both tests were selected and run.

| Phase | Backend (6 files) | E2E `agent-launch-host-switch-fresh.spec.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 35/35 passed, exit 0 | 2/2 passed (2704 ms, 3240 ms), phase completed |
| Fault | **35/35 passed, exit 0** | **2/2 failed**, exit 1 |
| Restored | 35/35 passed, exit 0 | 2/2 passed (2201 ms, 2091 ms), phase completed |

## What caught it, and what showed the wrong behavior
- `e2e/launches/agent-launch-host-switch-fresh.spec.ts:135`, "story launch Host switch shows Codex options observed after the switch without waiting for the poll": `expect(codexDialog.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Option B" })).toBeVisible()` failed (element not found).
- `e2e/launches/agent-launch-host-switch-fresh.spec.ts:195`, "Start session Host switch shows the Codex offer installed after the page's read...": the poll for a fresh ask whose answer offers Codex Start session timed out (false).
- The wrong behavior was observed on the intended path, separately from the assertions. Playwright's error-context page snapshots from the failed run show this:
  - The story-launch case shows the dialog "Start refinement in Codex" with Host=Codex selected. It still offers only `checkbox "Option A"`, which is the stale held observation; Option B, installed before the switch, is missing.
  - The Start-session case shows the dialog "Start a session in Open Dough in Codex" with `radio "Isolated workspace" [disabled]` and the paragraph "Isolated workspace and Automatically land are not offered...". The execution skill installed before the switch was not observed.
  - With the edit removed, the same runs pass, so the fault alone caused the failures.
- The backend specs give no verdict on this fault. `agent-launch-sessions-encoding.spec.ts` (admission) and `agent-launch-sessions-fresh.spec.ts` (`answerFor`) prove each side separately, and no backend spec in the set goes through `launchBoundaryAnswer.ts`. That is why they stayed green: they never run the adapter join that was faulted. For this story's promise at the HTTP adapter, the e2e spec is the only check among those examined that holds the proof the old started-server spec used to give.

## Restoration
After the trap restored the file, `git status --short` was empty, `git diff --quiet` succeeded, and HEAD was still `0c7ad7e2c`. The restored reruns of both commands passed, as the table shows. The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force` on that exact path, and `git worktree list` no longer shows it. The repository checkout was not edited.

## Next proof action
None required for this promise at this revision: the e2e check catches the dropped `fresh` at the adapter. Optional: if the coordinator wants this caught outside e2e, a backend check that drives `launchBoundaryAnswer`'s `sessions` case end to end would catch it more cheaply. That is a design choice for the plan owner and not a gap this probe found.

## Prior disposition
This matches the plan's relocation, where the adapter join is left to the e2e host-switch journey. The probe confirms that relocation holds and calls for no new repair.

## Setup and waiting problems
- `npm run test:e2e` prints nothing when the run passes (quiet reporter), so the baseline needed `OPEN_DOUGH_E2E_PROOF_RECORD` to prove both tests actually ran. One run without the record was discarded as non-evidence.
- Host load was about 11.5 (1-minute average) at the start. There were no flakes and no waiting stalls.

## Cost
- **Test runtime.** Measured from test-runner and wall-clock readings. Backend: Vitest reported 1.80 s baseline, 0.94 s faulted and 0.97 s restored. E2E: per-test durations from the proof record were 2.7 s + 3.2 s baseline, 7.1 s + 6.8 s faulted (failing at the 5 s expect timeouts) and 2.2 s + 2.1 s restored. The baseline e2e invocation took about 9 s wall-clock, including global setup, and the faulted one about 17 s.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no human took part, and there is nothing separate to measure.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no token or step meter is exposed to this agent. The only supported figure is the elapsed interval below.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 167644 ms (measured), from 1795600771000 to 1795600938644 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision 0c7ad7e2c6019d0b736e8e04ff4218ee61944e10: Caught by e2e/launches/agent-launch-host-switch-fresh.spec.ts; no follow-up.
